## What is monitored

Early Warning is monitored as three things: the model's **ranking**, the **tiers** cut from
it, and the **triggers** beside it. Each new cohort of booked accounts is scored by the
committed model — out-of-sample, unlike most of the development book — compared with the
held-out development accounts and, once its outcomes mature, measured against the development
performance. The thresholds are policy constants (`wiki/facts/policy.py`) and the model's own
gate, printed here by name. Events, for the calibration floor, are deteriorations.

| Metric | Population | Threshold | Frequency | Action on breach |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Top-decile capture | the cohort's accounts with matured outcomes | below the gate, {{< var ews.gate.capture_min >}} | when outcomes mature | One cohort below: review with the validator, reading the interval (finding 3). Two consecutive cohorts below: redevelopment ([7.9](gate.qmd)). |
| PR-AUC, and PR-AUC over the base rate | the same | at or below the cohort's base rate; a fall in the multiple from its development value | when outcomes mature | At or below the base rate: redevelopment. A falling multiple: review. |
| AUC | the same | below the sanity floor, {{< var ews.gate.auc_floor >}}; otherwise reported, not thresholded | when outcomes mature | Below the floor: redevelopment. Read against the ceiling, never against an origination AUC. |
| Benchmark against `pd_score` alone | the same | the model's capture or AUC at or below the score's | when outcomes mature | Review whether the behavioural model is still earning its place (finding 4). |
| Tier mix: PSI over High / Medium / Low | new accounts against the intended mix ({{< var ews.tier.High.share >}} / {{< var ews.tier.Medium.share >}} / {{< var ews.tier.Low.share >}}) | below {{< var monitoring.psi_watch >}} stable; {{< var monitoring.psi_watch >}} to {{< var monitoring.psi_act >}} watch; above {{< var monitoring.psi_act >}} act | every cohort | Watch: tell the review team its High-tier volume will differ from plan. Act: review with the validator (finding 1). |
| Observed / predicted deterioration rate, by tier | accounts with matured outcomes | outside {{< var monitoring.ratio_lo >}} to {{< var monitoring.ratio_hi >}}, on at least {{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}} deteriorations | when outcomes mature | Below the floor: record and watch. At or above it: count toward trigger 3. |
| Observed deterioration rate, by tier | accounts with matured outcomes | High not above Medium, or Medium not above Low | when outcomes mature | The tiers no longer rank: review with the validator. |
| Trigger fire share, each trigger | every account scored | any trigger's share moving by more than {{< var monitoring.rule_hit_move >}} of its development share | every scoring run | Check the feature's source before the rule; report to the monitoring policy owner (proposed; to be named). |
| Trigger clauses firing alone | every account scored | any clause that fires on no account by itself | every scoring run | Report as an untested control (finding 6). |
| Trigger precision, each trigger | accounts with matured outcomes | reported against the base rate, not thresholded | when outcomes mature | Read with finding 7's threshold review. |
| Tier cutoffs at a retrain | the retrained model | any change | every retrain | The workload was held and the risk accepted moved: the policy owner signs off the new cutoffs before use ([7.4](assumptions.qmd#ews-tiers-as-a-fixed-mix)). |
| Watchlist: share of training rows | the watchlist served | reported, not thresholded | every scoring run | Any training row on the list makes its hit rate in-sample (finding 2). |

The capture row is the gate carried into production, with the one-and-two-cohorts rule that
finding 3 needs: on the development sample, {{< var ews.boot.capture_below_gate >}} of
bootstrap resamples fall below the gate with nothing wrong, so a single breach is evidence to
read, not yet a verdict. The first capture reading on a cohort whose outcomes mature after its
features were taken is also the model's first out-of-time test, and the first measurement of
lead time (finding 8). The tier-mix row is the control for finding 1, the calibration row
for finding 5, the trigger rows for findings 6 and 7, the watchlist row for finding 2 and the
benchmark row for finding 4.

## Trigger fire rates and dead clauses {#ews-trigger-monitoring}

A trigger clause that never fires is a control that cannot be shown to work. The detection is
the count of accounts each clause flags by itself — the facts compute it by running
`flag_triggers` with every other feature zeroed — on every scoring run. At development one
clause is already dead ({{< var ews.trigger.n_dead_clauses >}}): `DELINQUENCY`'s `dpd_max`
clause (finding 6). It is flagged from the first cohort and stays flagged until the policy
owner restates or removes it. A clause that *stops* firing after firing at development is a
stronger signal: a feature whose definition or source has changed. The share row uses the same
relative threshold as adjudication's rule hits (D5.8), because a trigger is a rule.

The tier mix already sits in the watch band at development (finding 1), the Low tier is
already outside the calibration tolerance (finding 5), and one clause is already dead
(finding 6): the first cohorts are read against those three rows before any other.

## Redevelopment triggers {#ews-redevelopment-triggers}

Any one of these starts a redevelopment, with the validator informed:

1. Top-decile capture below the gate in two consecutive cohorts with matured outcomes, or
   PR-AUC at or below the base rate, or AUC below the sanity floor, in any one.
2. Tier-mix PSI above {{< var monitoring.psi_act >}}.
3. A tier's observed / predicted ratio outside the tolerance in two consecutive cohorts, each
   with at least {{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}} deteriorations behind that tier.
   Below that count a breach is recorded and watched, not acted on. The Low tier already
   breaches at development (finding 5).
4. A change to any input's definition or source — including any change to the scorecard,
   which supplies two inputs ([D3](../d3-dependencies.qmd#what-a-scorecard-change-forces)),
   and to the panel.

Two further events go to the monitoring policy owner (proposed; to be named) rather than to redevelopment: a change to
any value in `EWS_TRIGGERS`, after which [7.5](performance.qmd#ews-trigger-performance) is
re-run; and a clause that fires on no account (above).

A redevelopment is also where the open findings of [7.7](limitations.qmd) are acted on, and
where the questions this chapter leaves open are answered: whether the behavioural model earns
its place beside `pd_score` alone, with paired intervals on capture (finding 4); how it
performs refitted without the score and without the panel
([7.6](sensitivity.qmd#reduced-input-refits-not-run)); what out-of-sample cutoffs and a
calibration step do to the tiers (findings 1 and 5); and the threshold sweep the triggers need
(finding 7). Every redevelopment re-runs [7.5](performance.qmd) and passes the gate.

## What is automated today

This plan is documented, not yet automated. The platform has one booked book and one draw of
outcomes, so there is no new cohort to compare. What runs today is the development side:
`python verify.py` recomputes the held-out capture, PR-AUC and AUC against its own copies of
the gate ([7.9](gate.qmd)), and on `main` recomputes every fact on these pages — the tier mix,
each clause's firings alone, the watchlist's composition — from the committed model and data
on every run ([D9](../d9-implementation.qmd)). A dead clause is visible in the generated
trigger table on every build, but nothing yet fails on it.
